title: Research: exact two-port clean-cache cost obstruction
body:
## Result

A clean scratch cache that carries one read-only source contribution across exactly two output ports cannot improve the local transport bill when both the load and exact restore are charged. For source, scratch, and output frames F,H,G_j, let a=dim(F+H), b_j=dim(H+G_j), and d_j=dim(F+G_j). The dimension identity gives a+b_j >= d_j. For every 0<s<1, monotonicity and subadditivity give d_j^s <= a^s+b_j^s. Summing over two ports proves

```text
cache  = 2*a^s + b_1^s + b_2^s
       >= d_1^s + d_2^s = direct.
```

The result screens one-source/two-output routing only. The direct term is an optimistic local comparator, not a claim that those two channel transfers form a legal full supplier. This does not rule out multi-source coding, changed support or frames, or another nine-array program, and it makes no supplier-admission or new-kappa claim.

A Q^15 coordinate-span control has a=6, b_j=8, d_j=13. At s=9983/10000 the exact intervals show the two-output cache costs 27.907043 versus 25.886876 direct, while for three outputs the cache costs 35.878812 versus 38.830314 direct. This confirms the port-count restriction matters. A separate negative control shows that omitting restoration would falsely predict a two-port saving.
